nodes.label: bedrock-mantle transport
nodes.rationale: AWS-recommended route and the ONLY one Gemma 4 31B supports. Configured alongside bedrock-runtime so Phase 0 can pick per arm from evidence rather than assumption, and so an adapter failure can be told apart from model weakness (spec section 6.4). Authenticates by explicit api_key on each deployment, which takes base_aws_llm.get_request_headers' api_key branch.

nodes.label: bedrock-runtime transport
nodes.rationale: Two routes wearing one prefix, chosen by model id rather than by anything in the config file. Claude models resolve to AmazonAnthropicClaudeMessagesConfig and take Invoke with a native Anthropic body, never constructing a toolUseId; everything else falls through to the openai->Converse bridge, which copies the model's own tool-call ids verbatim into toolUseId under a [a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64} class Bedrock enforces server-side. Carries no api_key so SigV4 signing is used.

nodes.label: claude-sonnet-5 deployment (mantle)
nodes.rationale: api_base deliberately omits the /v1 the endpoint actually serves: LiteLLM's anthropic provider appends '/v1/messages' itself, so the documented .../anthropic/v1 base produces a doubled /v1/v1/messages and 404s with an empty error body. Temperature/top_p/top_k are OMITTED because any non-default value returns 400 on this model, which would fail every call on the reference arm.

nodes.label: gemma-4-31b deployment (mantle)
nodes.rationale: Mantle only -- Gemma supports neither Converse nor Invoke, and its path is /openai/v1 rather than /v1. top_p is omitted under force: on 2026-08-12 the route began validating this model under OpenAI's reasoning-model contract, which rejects any non-default top_p outright, while temperature 1.0 passes and 0.6 does not. Section 5.3's constant across arms is the POLICY (lab-recommended unless the route refuses it), not the number, which is why nemotron and kimi keep top_p 0.95 rather than being levelled down. Reasoning content is returned only by the Responses API, so TokenUsage.reasoning reads zero on this path.

nodes.label: nemotron-3-super-120b deployment (mantle)
nodes.rationale: temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 per NVIDIA's published guidance for all tasks; path is /v1 (OpenAI Chat Completions).

nodes.label: kimi-k2-5 deployment (mantle)
nodes.rationale: temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 for thinking mode; Moonshot documents temperature 0 causing multi-minute stalls, which is why a single uniform sampling number across arms would be a section 5.4 failure mode.

nodes.label: claude-sonnet-5-runtime deployment
nodes.rationale: Must use the us. geo inference profile: the model card lists the In-Region runtime URL as N/A, so the bare ID cannot be invoked. US geo also matches the data-residency posture behind choosing Bedrock. No temperature/top_p -- same 400 as the mantle arm.

nodes.label: kimi-k2-5-runtime deployment (commented out)
nodes.rationale: Commented out, not deleted: it is the fallback transport if mantle ever breaks for Kimi the way it broke for Sonnet, and what it would take to restore it is worth keeping next to it. It cannot be served as written -- Kimi's tool-call ids are `functions.Read:0`, litellm sanitizes tool NAMES on the Converse path and never ids, and bakeoff.litellm_patches deliberately removed the id sanitizer (removing it is what let Kimi drive the tool loop at all), so this deployment would send a colon to Converse and fail server-side. Leaving it live left it one `--models kimi-k2-5-runtime` away from a paid run. Restoring requires an allowlist entry in CONVERSE_SAFE_TOOL_ID_MODELS with the measured id shape as evidence.

nodes.label: BAKEOFF_MANTLE_TOKEN env var name
nodes.rationale: The env var NAME is load-bearing because one proxy serves both transports. base_aws_llm.get_request_headers (verified litellm 1.95.0) uses a deployment's api_key when set, falls back to AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, and signs SigV4 only when both are absent. A proxy process with AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK set would bearer-authenticate the runtime deployments and fail every runtime arm with `bedrock:CallWithBearerToken`, while the mantle arms stay green -- reading as a bedrock-runtime problem. BAKEOFF_MANTLE_TOKEN is a name LiteLLM does not look up, so the mantle deployments name it explicitly and the runtime deployments find nothing and sign.

nodes.label: Every model_name must be distinct
nodes.rationale: LiteLLM treats repeated model_name values as one load-balanced deployment group and round-robins between them, which would randomize transport per call and confound both latency and tool-translation results. model_name also doubles as the PRICE_BOOK key in bakeoff.costs, so a name the price book does not know raises UnknownModelError mid-run. A third consequence: every model group is therefore single-deployment, which is what makes the router cooldown useless here.

nodes.label: Lab-recommended sampling policy (section 5.3)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code has no temperature flag, so the proxy config is the only layer that can set sampling. Section 5.3 says '0.6 (or lab-recommended)'; lab-recommended is what is used because a single uniform number would 400 the Sonnet arm and stall Kimi -- a config choice scored as a model difference (section 5.4). The constant held across arms is the policy, not the value, which is why config_digest deliberately excludes temperature. NOT VERIFIED in this file: LiteLLM merges litellm_params as defaults and Claude Code's own body may win, so only the wire log shows what was actually sent.

nodes.label: litellm_settings.callbacks registration (production)
nodes.rationale: Wire capture must be registered where the calls are actually made (section 6.2): the agent runs in its own container and the proxy is a third process, so a callback registered in the harness process observes nothing -- Task 11's defect 15, which produced records with empty sampling, empty prompt and tool hashes and no error status while looking complete. The dotted path must resolve to a module-level INSTANCE: get_instance_fn resolves the path with getattr and returns it as-is, then success_handler dispatches on isinstance(callback, CustomLogger), so a class object is skipped in SILENCE. bakeoff.wire.BakeoffCallback additionally cannot be named here because it needs a per-run WireLogger and run_id no config string can supply.

nodes.label: use_chat_completions_url_for_anthropic_messages
nodes.rationale: Without it LiteLLM sends any openai/ deployment's Anthropic Messages traffic to the Responses API and Bedrock answers 400 ('does not support the /v1/responses API'), measured on the Phase 0c live run 2026-08-07 for both Nemotron and Kimi. A section 6.4 adapter setting, not a model finding: the failure was identical on every candidate arm and would have read as three models unable to drive Claude Code.

nodes.label: additional_drop_params (named one at a time)
nodes.rationale: Never a blanket drop_params: true -- that would silently discard temperature or max_tokens if a provider rejected one, leaving section 5.3 sampling unapplied with nothing in the record saying so. context_management and output_config are turned into an anthropic-beta header by LiteLLM and mantle answers 'invalid beta flag'. CORRECTION 2026-08-12: reasoning_effort was NOT a Bedrock rejection -- probed with raw httpx, Bedrock ACCEPTS it on all three candidates and 'high' measurably changes output (gemma 240->580, kimi 171->717 completion tokens). The rejection is litellm's own _check_valid_arg because OpenAIGPTConfig.get_supported_openai_params omits it for a non-o-series model. The entry is kept as a backstop so a patch that fails to apply produces a loud UnsupportedParamsError rather than silently forwarding the 'medium' litellm derives from Claude Code's thinking: {type: adaptive}.

nodes.label: router_settings.disable_cooldowns (production)
nodes.rationale: Measured against litellm 1.95.0: _should_cooldown_deployment has four branches, three guarded by is_single_deployment_model_group and the fourth (elif litellm._should_retry(status_code) is False) is not. _should_retry(401) and (403) are both False, so ONE auth failure cools the deployment down for 5 s. Every model group is single-deployment by design, so there is nothing to fail over to; num_retries: 3 then retries into the cooldown and gets RouterRateLimitError, a plain ValueError with NO status_code, so the wire log's last entry reads 'No deployments available' at status None instead of naming the credential problem. The other unguarded branch needs 1000 requests in a minute and is unreachable. Applied to every deployment identically, so not a section 5.3 divergence.

nodes.label: general_settings.num_retries: 3
nodes.rationale: Retries are logged as infra events, never silently absorbed. Each retry is its own callback invocation, which is why the wire log counts calls rather than turns.

nodes.label: bakeoff.proxy_callback.instance
nodes.rationale: Exists as a module-level object precisely so a config line can point at an instance rather than a type -- LiteLLM's get_instance_fn resolves the dotted path with getattr and dispatches on isinstance(callback, CustomLogger), skipping a class in silence. Attributes each call by the X-Bakeoff-Run-Id header the harness stamps per run; the harness replays those lines through WireLogger afterwards so there is exactly one canonical artifact.

nodes.label: bakeoff.litellm_patches.instance
nodes.rationale: Applies its patches on construction and is imported by nothing in the harness -- that separation is what keeps the harness process's litellm unpatched. Not optional in ANY config: the tool-id patch must be present wherever a proxy is started, or the offline gate and the fault-injection suite certify an UNPATCHED topology under the same name as the patched one. Carries the max_tokens->max_completion_tokens rename and the reasoning_effort='none' pin, neither of which can be expressed in config because a drop cannot express a value.

nodes.label: mock-throttle deployment (429 -> api_throttle)
nodes.rationale: mock_response carries the sentinel string 'litellm.RateLimitError', which litellm's /v1/messages route recognises and raises as a REAL exception carrying status 429 -- the status classify_exclusion maps to the pre-registered reason api_throttle.

nodes.label: mock-5xx deployment (500 -> api_5xx)
nodes.rationale: Raises litellm.InternalServerError at status 500, which classify_exclusion maps to api_5xx.

nodes.label: mock_response sentinel exceptions
nodes.rationale: The error deployments raise REAL exceptions, not canned error bodies. Verified in litellm 1.95.0 (llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/utils.py): three sentinel strings are recognised on the /v1/messages route and raise the corresponding litellm exception carrying the status code classify_exclusion maps to a reason. RateLimitError 429 -> api_throttle, InternalServerError 500 -> api_5xx, ContextWindowExceededError 400 -> not an infra failure by design. There is no sentinel for Timeout (408), so that branch stays unit-tested -- stated rather than left as an apparent gap. Answering from mock_response is what lets the whole capture path run with no credentials and no spend, because a gate that costs money is a gate that stops being run.

nodes.label: num_retries: 0 in the fault-injection config
nodes.rationale: Deliberately unlike production. A retry would turn one injected 429 into four wire entries and make the test assert on retry behaviour instead of on capture. The retry-versus-final-error rule is covered by its own unit test.

nodes.label: router_settings.disable_cooldowns (fault injection)
nodes.rationale: Verbatim copy of the production rationale, so the gate exercises the same router behaviour it certifies.

nodes.label: claude-sonnet-5 offline arm
nodes.rationale: Named claude-sonnet-5 -- a REAL arm name -- on purpose, because model_name doubles as the PRICE_BOOK key: a name like mock-ok raises UnknownModelError inside cost_usd, assemble_record catches it, and the record's turns/tokens/cost are all zero with only trajectory_parse_error set, so the offline gate would be measuring the price book rather than the topology. api_base carries neither /v1/messages nor a trailing /v1 because LiteLLM's anthropic provider appends it, exactly as the mantle Sonnet arm does.

nodes.label: gemma-4-31b offline arm (sampling probe)
nodes.rationale: Exists to carry sampling. Section 5.3 puts sampling entirely in proxy config because Claude Code has no temperature flag, and Task 11 could not tell whether a deployment-level temperature survives to the wire -- it was absent from optional_params, litellm_params and standard_logging_object on the mock path, which short-circuits before provider param transformation. A real provider call answers the question, and this arm asks it for free. Values match the production gemma arm so the answer transfers.

nodes.label: kimi-k2-5 offline arm (tool-id patch detector)
nodes.rationale: The only offline arm that reaches the openai->anthropic adapter. The two anthropic/ arms bypass it entirely, so the 2026-08-07 tool-id defect -- LiteLLM rewriting Kimi's `functions.Read:0` to `functions_Read_0` and breaking its tool loop -- was structurally invisible to this gate and cost a live run to find. The stub answers with a Kimi-shaped tool_call id and REJECTS a tool_call_id it never issued, so if bakeoff.litellm_patches stops applying the id comes back mangled, the stub 400s, and this arm goes red -- the only way the gate can tell a live patch from a dead one. Carries additional_drop_params per deployment because the global litellm_settings entry measurably does NOT reach an openai/ deployment's param validation.

nodes.label: mock_response short-circuits the streaming callback
nodes.rationale: LiteLLM's mock short-circuits inside anthropic_messages before the provider call, so a STREAMING request never reaches the streaming wrapper that fires the success callback on stream completion. Measured against litellm 1.95.0 with claude 2.1.220: two calls made, only the non-streaming one captured. Every real Claude Code call is streaming, so a gate built on mocks would certify capture that does not happen -- the same class of defect as Task 11's defect 15.

nodes.label: Offline gate must mirror production settings
nodes.rationale: use_chat_completions_url_for_anthropic_messages, additional_drop_params and num_retries are mirrored from litellm_config.yaml, because a setting that differs between the two files is a section 5.2 divergence in the gate itself -- the offline gate would exercise different routing than the run it is meant to certify.
nodes.norm_label: offline gate must mirror production settings

nodes.label: Phase 0c smoke task fixture
nodes.rationale: The smallest task that still exercises the whole loop: read a failing test, locate a one-character bug (`add` returns `a - b`), edit a file, and run the test to see it pass.

nodes.label: The agent must be able to run the test and see it pass
nodes.rationale: pytest.ini is what makes `from calc import add` resolve and the eval image is what supplies pytest. Break either and the fixture is red before the fix and red after it, so a correct run and an idle run leave identical evidence -- which is how Phase 0c scored an environment defect as a model failure. The remedy is to verify the fixture itself (`pytest -q` fails, change calc.py to `a + b`, `pytest -q` passes), not just the harness.
nodes.norm_label: the agent must be able to run the test and see it pass

nodes.label: The smoke task directory is a template, not a git repository
nodes.rationale: scripts/smoke_test.py copies it under $HOME and runs `git init` there at run time, deriving base_sha from the commit it just made. Committing it with a .git inside would make git record an embedded-repo gitlink rather than the files, and a hand-written base_sha would go stale the first time the fixture changed.
nodes.norm_label: the smoke task directory is a template, not a git repository

nodes.label: Layer 1 - refused by code
nodes.rationale: The only layer enforced mechanically. Nothing here needs judgment: run `run_matrix.py --preflight-only --tasks <task_id>` and read the output. Offline, no credentials, no spend; needs Docker and, the first time a repo is mirrored, network. The asymmetry that sets the bar: a refused task costs a message, an accepted-wrongly task costs a matrix -- every arm scored on an unverifiable guess, in an append-only log.

nodes.label: Layer 2 - required, and nothing checks it
nodes.rationale: Where a task set goes wrong quietly: every item produces a task that passes Layer 1 and measures the wrong thing. Covers the oracle (behaviour not internals, no property-based suites, determinism), provenance (base_sha, verbatim reference, licence), the prompt (verbatim, no replayed human corrections), and the image (no submodules, no VCS-derived version, suite fast enough).
nodes.norm_label: layer 2 - required, and nothing checks it

nodes.label: Layer 3 - properties of the set, not of any task
nodes.rationale: ~80 harvested to land ~60 (section 3.5), stratified to the MEASURED production distribution rather than a guessed split -- a 50/50 split on a workload that is 70% small edits measures the wrong thing and will not transfer to the bill. Must include a long-session stratum because all three candidates claim 256K context, degrade unevenly well before it, and small tasks never surface that.
nodes.norm_label: layer 3 - properties of the set, not of any task

nodes.label: Tests assert behaviour, not internal names
nodes.rationale: The single most important judgment call per candidate, and no gate catches it. click #3678 was rejected for exactly this: its tests pin an arbitrary storage name, so a different-but-correct fix would be scored as a failure. Prefer tests that compare rendered output, return values, or raised messages.
nodes.norm_label: tests assert behaviour, not internal names

nodes.label: No property-based oracle
nodes.rationale: A hypothesis-driven suite can pass a wrong fix on a lucky draw and fail a right one on an unlucky seed; attrs and cattrs are excluded for this. The suite must also be deterministic -- preflight runs p2p twice, so a flake makes the gate a coin flip and the eval unreproducible.

nodes.label: base_sha is merge_commit^1
nodes.rationale: The real parent of the merge, not the PR's recorded base.sha. The base branch advances between a PR being opened and merged, and diffing against the stale one puts unrelated commits into the reference. Measured on click #3434: 7c99ebe -> 63274a7.

nodes.label: The reference is the real merged PR, verbatim
nodes.rationale: Section 3.2, without exception. It converts the judge's question from open-ended 'is this diff good?' (kappa ~ 0.32, below the 0.6 acceptability bar) into reference-anchored 'does this accomplish what the reference accomplished?'. The licence must permit redistributing the diff and the prompt.
nodes.norm_label: the reference is the real merged pr, verbatim

nodes.label: The prompt is verbatim
nodes.rationale: Section 3.3: the issue title, then the issue body exactly as filed, plus the ticket description where one exists. Nothing added -- a harness-authored sentence ('the tests are in tests/', 'do not edit the tests') makes it a different task from the one a human actually opened, and this eval exists to measure the workflow that happens rather than a tidied one. Human corrections are not replayed because a follow-up like 'fix the import on line 40' was conditioned on the original model's output and is incoherent against a candidate that wrote different code.

nodes.label: rubric_items from unreplayed human corrections
nodes.rationale: Human follow-up turns that cannot be replayed become rubric_items instead -- a free, human-authored list of what 'done' required.

nodes.label: Three silent task-image build failures
nodes.rationale: All found by screening rather than reasoning. (1) No git submodules -- the build context is `git archive base_sha`, which drops them, so tomlkit cannot collect its suite. (2) No VCS-derived version unless build: supplies a pretend-version -- git archive leaves no .git and setuptools_scm refuses; measured across 12 candidates only setuptools_scm is strict, hatch-vcs builds fine. (3) The suite must be fast enough: preflight runs it four times under a 600 s timeout and the agent re-runs it inside wall_clock_timeout_s, so ~40 s is the practical ceiling and click's 1.4 s is what comfortable looks like.

nodes.label: Pruned run tree shortens the abbreviated SHA
nodes.rationale: Tags that are ancestors of base_sha survive the prune, so `git describe` still resolves and setuptools_scm/hatch-vcs can still derive a version. But core.abbrev auto-sizes to the smaller object count, so 8.3.3-69-g63274a79 becomes 8.3.3-69-g63274a7 (measured) -- a package installed at image-build time and one the agent rebuilds in the run tree disagree on version string. Nothing asserts this; preflight already runs the suite inside the image, so a mismatch that breaks anything surfaces there.
nodes.norm_label: pruned run tree shortens the abbreviated sha

nodes.label: The model-neutral drop rule
nodes.rationale: Drop only if ALL four models score 0% (floor -- usually underspecified rather than hard) or ALL four score 100% (ceiling -- no signal). Keep every disagreement, however lopsided: a task only Sonnet solves is among the most informative in the set. Read against the measured variance: on 2026-08-13 this task set's one task went 4/4 resolved and then 2/4 on the same four arms hours apart at temperature 1.0 and N=1 -- between-run variance larger than the between-arm spread. At N=3 a discriminating task can present as a floor, which is an argument for more repeats in the pilot, not for a looser drop rule.

nodes.label: Calibration pilot before freeze
nodes.rationale: All four models, N=3, across every candidate. Selecting tasks by one model's difficulty curve tilts the set toward what that model happens to discriminate on, which is precisely the bias this eval exists to avoid.

nodes.label: task_version bumps on any edit
nodes.rationale: It is not part of run_id, so an edited task leaves every finished cell looking complete while mixing two different tasks under one task_id. Resume hard-refuses on the mismatch, per cell.

nodes.label: Screened repository list
nodes.rationale: Measured 2026-08-13 in python:3.12-slim-bookworm: editable install, git clean -xfd, full suite, then git status. Suite times are at HEAD, NOT at any candidate's base_sha -- green here does not guarantee green there, and preflight remains the gate. The PR column counts merged PRs linked to an issue created after 2024-01-01 and is an availability proxy only. Excluded: tomlkit (submodule dropped by git archive), attrs/cattrs (hypothesis suites plus a site-packages `attr` collision), python-slugify (no harvestable PRs).

nodes.label: sqlglot base_sha date constraint
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md was added 2026-02-02 (a65c8701a306, PR #6899) and AGENTS.md followed 2026-03-19 (7f0dd47f60a3), with a later commit making CLAUDE.md a symlink to it. Both are present at HEAD and preflight's `test -e` follows symlinks, so base_sha must predate 2026-02-02. That leaves 680 clean candidates against 116 after the cutoff -- the constraint costs almost nothing and sqlglot remains the richest source by an order of magnitude. A SQL transpiler is also close to the ideal bug shape: input SQL, exact expected output, tests that assert rendered strings rather than internal names.

nodes.label: Pinned reference.diff cut flags
nodes.rationale: `git -c diff.noprefix=false -c diff.renames=true diff --binary <base_sha> <merge_commit>`. Not cosmetic: without them the diff's SHAPE is a property of the harvester's ~/.gitconfig rather than of the task, and 80 references cut on different machines would not be the same kind of object. noprefix=false because a --no-prefix diff is refused at load (git apply's -p1 would strip a REAL path component and silently swap which files are the oracle); renames=true because `copies` turns plain modifications into copy chunks; --binary because a plain git diff renders a binary change as 'Binary files ... differ' with no payload, which loads clean and then fails in preflight. Leave core.quotepath at its default -- quoted headers are never parsed for paths, and turning it off writes raw non-UTF-8 bytes that fail to decode at load.

nodes.label: Cutting one - the harvest procedure
nodes.rationale: Read the tests FIRST -- Layer 2's behaviour-not-internals rule disqualifies most candidates and is cheapest to check before anything else. Leave repo.start_sha out on the first pass and pin the value the gate reports. Run the f2p tests by hand at the start state to get node ids right -- they are measured, never guessed. Iterate --preflight-only until it prints PASS, because every problem it reports maps to a defect that would otherwise read as model capability.

nodes.label: click-3360 repo pinning (base_sha / start_sha)
nodes.rationale: base_sha 63274a79 is merge_commit^1, not the PR's recorded base.sha -- the base branch advanced from 7c99ebe to 63274a7 between the PR being opened and merged, and diffing against the stale one would put unrelated commits into the reference. start_sha 33575cc0 is base_sha plus the test half committed with a fixed identity and date, pinned so that a re-cut patch or a different git moving the start state is a load error rather than a silent change to what every arm was asked to do.

nodes.label: click-3360 verbatim issue prompt
nodes.rationale: Section 3.3: the issue title then the body exactly as filed, including the reporter's HTML template comment. Nothing added -- a harness-authored sentence would be a different task from the one a human actually opened. Subject: HelpFormatter.write_usage produces an empty Usage line when no args are passed.

nodes.label: click-3360 f2p test set
nodes.rationale: Measured, not guessed: exactly the tests that fail at the start state and pass after the reference fix. They assert rendered output rather than any internal name, so a different-but-correct fix passes -- which is why this PR was chosen over #3678, whose tests pin an arbitrary storage name. p2p is deliberately empty (everything else the runner collects, 1,615 tests at this base_sha, green before and after); an explicit list would go stale against a pinned suite for no benefit. The runner passes `-p no:cacheprovider` so the suite writes no .pytest_cache into the tree, because section 5.6 stages everything.

nodes.label: click-3360 allow_extra_paths (CHANGES.rst)
nodes.rationale: Files in the merged PR that belong to NEITHER half. The changelog entry cites :issue:`3360` :pr:`3434` -- no agent will write that, so leaving it in the solution half makes preflight apply documentation it does not need and would make any later diff-similarity metric measure changelog authorship. Explicit rather than inferred: nothing available at load time can tell a changelog from a source file, so an UNLISTED extra file still lands in the fix half exactly as before.

nodes.label: click-3360 image block (less, pytest 8.3.5, editable install)
nodes.rationale: apt: less because it is a TEST dependency and the base image ships no pager -- test_echo_via_pager parametrizes over ['cat','less',...] and with no less on PATH the pager path closes the borrowed stdout, so pytest's capfd raises 'I/O operation on closed file' in setup AND teardown of every remaining test in the file: 189 errors, none about the code under test, and it does not reproduce on macOS. pip: pytest==8.3.5 because the base image pins pytest 9.1.1 and click sets filterwarnings=['error'], so pytest 9 raises PytestRemovedIn10Warning during collection and the suite exits 2 -- red before AND after any fix; upstream fixed it in #3656, two months after this base_sha. build must be EDITABLE: a plain `pip install .` resolves imports to site-packages so nothing the agent writes to /repo takes effect and every arm fails identically.
nodes.norm_label: click-3360 image block (less, pytest 8.3.5, editable install)

nodes.label: click-3360 budget placeholders
nodes.rationale: max_turns 40 / wall_clock_timeout_s 900 are section 5.4 placeholders. Real caps come from the section 3.5 calibration pilot's slowest-converging model, not from the incumbent.

nodes.label: click-3360 provenance (Tier B)
nodes.rationale: Tier B (section 3.2): a tested PR with no transcript -- the oracle is executable and the merged PR is the reference diff. pallets/click issue 3360, PR 3434, merge_commit 3bb230dc, merged 2026-05-16, BSD-3-Clause. session_id and original_model are explicitly null rather than omitted, because no transcript exists for this work.

nodes.label: Cost-Efficient LLM Bakeoff for Agentic Coding
nodes.author: Suhaas Surapaneni
nodes.rationale: Business-facing plan doc: selects a lower-cost Bedrock model to replace Claude Sonnet 5 for agentic coding at Pindrop. Recommends a ~2-2.5 week internal bakeoff because no public benchmark cleanly covers all three candidates.
nodes.norm_label: cost-efficient llm bakeoff for agentic coding

nodes.label: Model Bakeoff Plan (rendered PDF)
nodes.author: Suhaas Surapaneni
nodes.rationale: Typeset export of Model_Bakeoff_Plan.md, same content and same July 29 2026 refresh date; exists as the shareable artifact for stakeholders rather than as a separate source of truth.

nodes.label: Kimi K2.5
nodes.rationale: Candidate arm. Leads on the vendor-reported SWE-bench Verified (76.8%) and on AA indices, but the one independent test (Terminal-Bench Hard, 34.8%) puts it below Gemma -- treated as a hypothesis, not a fact. 16K output ceiling risks truncation on large diffs; modified-MIT license needs legal sign-off. Saves only ~80-82%.

nodes.label: Nemotron 3 Super 120B
nodes.rationale: Candidate arm at $0.15/$0.65 with the largest output ceiling (32K). NVIDIA is the only vendor here disclosing multiple harness variants (53.7-60.5%) rather than one cherry-picked number, which is treated as a credibility signal despite the weakest headline score.

nodes.label: Gemma 4 31B
nodes.rationale: Cheapest candidate ($0.14/$0.40, ~96% savings), cleanest license (Apache 2.0), and leader among candidates on both independent benchmarks that cover it. No SWE-bench Verified score exists at all, and it is newest on Bedrock (June 2026) via the bedrock-mantle endpoint, so it carries the least production history.

nodes.label: Claude Sonnet 5 (incumbent reference)
nodes.rationale: The incumbent, priced $3.00/$15.00 standard tier and used as the $5,000/month cost baseline. Artificial Analysis found its cost per completed task runs ~15% above Opus 4.8 despite a lower per-token price, which is the evidence for deciding on cost per completed workflow rather than per token.

nodes.label: Self-hosted LiteLLM proxy as the access layer
nodes.rationale: One unified way to call and switch between all candidate models with built-in cost tracking, running inside Pindrop's own AWS account so no data passes through a third party.
nodes.norm_label: self-hosted litellm proxy as the access layer

nodes.label: OpenRouter rejected as routing layer
nodes.rationale: Even under Bring-Your-Own-Key, requests still transit OpenRouter's own servers before reaching Bedrock and carry a ~5% fee -- which cuts against the pricing and data-residency reasons Pindrop standardized on Bedrock in the first place.

nodes.label: SWE-bench Verified (contamination caveat)
nodes.rationale: Included because it is the only benchmark with real coverage, not because it is trustworthy: OpenAI stopped reporting it in Feb 2026 after an audit of 138 tasks found ~59% materially flawed and every frontier model tested had memorized the human-written fix.

nodes.label: Terminal-Bench Hard (independent agentic CLI)
nodes.rationale: The only independently-run benchmark covering two of the three candidates; its disagreement with vendor numbers (Kimi 34.8% independent vs 50.8% vendor on a different track) is the direct evidence that vendor claims cannot decide this.

nodes.label: Artificial Analysis Index scores
nodes.rationale: Independent composite (Intelligence Index, Coding Index, output speed) kept in its own table rather than mixed with task-specific benchmarks, because it is a different lens and blending the two would imply comparability that does not exist.

nodes.label: Cost per completed workflow
nodes.rationale: The decision metric, not cost per token: a model that burns tokens or retries to reach the same answer is not cheap. Grounded in AA's measurement that Sonnet 5 costs ~15% more per completed task than Opus 4.8 at a lower per-token price.

nodes.label: Two-tier internal eval set (Tier A bug fix / Tier B feature scale)
nodes.rationale: 40-60 tasks on real Pindrop repos, N>=3 samples graded blind. Tier B (multi-file) is where the recommendation is said to be won or lost, because no public benchmark has contamination-clean coverage of all three candidates.
nodes.norm_label: two-tier internal eval set (tier a bug fix / tier b feature scale)

nodes.label: bedrock-mantle endpoint
nodes.rationale: Gemma 4 31B is served here rather than on standard bedrock-runtime, which is why it does not appear under the console's Serverless model-catalog filter and why Phase 0 must confirm the endpoint per model.

nodes.label: Plan-doc success criteria and thresholds
nodes.rationale: Task completion >=90% of Sonnet 5 weighted to Tier B, terminal-command success >=95%, cross-file changes correct >=90%, cost <=40% of Sonnet 5 per completed workflow. The design spec later demotes these from gates to reference points.

nodes.label: LLM Bakeoff Eval Design Spec
nodes.author: Suhaas Surapaneni
nodes.rationale: The spec every `section N.N` reference in the codebase points at. Companion to Model_Bakeoff_Plan.md; it measures and does not decide, and its primary deliverable is an immutable event log rather than a score.

nodes.label: Model-neutrality rule
nodes.rationale: No experimental parameter may be calibrated to a single model. Where a value must come from somewhere it comes from the slowest or broadest case across all four arms, so no model is advantaged by having set the ruler. Sonnet 5 is an arm, not the answer key.

nodes.label: Primary deliverable: the immutable event log
nodes.rationale: Scores are derived views over the log. Re-running 2,000 agentic sessions is expensive and the models will have changed by then, but re-scoring a preserved log is free -- so any metric not captured at run time is lost permanently.
nodes.norm_label: primary deliverable: the immutable event log

nodes.label: Contamination-free private task set
nodes.rationale: An internal eval on Pindrop's private repos has one property no public benchmark has: the tasks have never been in any model's training data. Named as the strongest methodological claim available.

nodes.label: Four-source task join (ticket, PR, transcript, base_sha)
nodes.rationale: Branch name plus timestamp is the join key into PR history. Known gap: transcripts record gitBranch but no commit SHA, so exact codebase state is recovered lossily by correlating timestamps against git log -- a SessionStart hook stamping `git rev-parse HEAD` is the forward fix.
nodes.norm_label: four-source task join (ticket, pr, transcript, base_sha)

nodes.label: Task classes A gold / B mined / C agent-only
nodes.rationale: Every task carries the real merged PR diff as reference without exception, which converts the judge's question from open-ended 'is this diff good?' (Cohen's kappa ~0.32) into reference-anchored 'does this accomplish what the reference accomplished?'. The dataset, not the judge prompt, is what makes judging accurate.
nodes.norm_label: task classes a gold / b mined / c agent-only

nodes.label: One-instruction prompt construction
nodes.rationale: One human instruction, then autonomous turns: reads, edits, runs tests, sees failures, self-corrects. Multi-turn human corrections are not replayed because they were conditioned on the original model's output; they are repurposed as judge rubric items instead.

nodes.label: No LLM user-simulator
nodes.rationale: Rejected despite precedent (tau-bench, AA's tau3-Banking): it confounds model with simulator, and a useful simulator needs the answer, which leaks unevenly -- a floundering model draws more corrective detail, actively compensating weak models and inverting what the eval measures.

nodes.label: Stratification to measured production distribution
nodes.rationale: Weight strata to a measured transcript stats pass, not a guessed split -- a 50/50 tier split on a workload that is 70% small edits measures the wrong thing and will not transfer to the bill. Includes a long-session stratum because 256K context claims degrade unevenly before the limit.

nodes.label: Calibration pilot and model-neutral drop rule
nodes.rationale: All four models at N=3 across ~80 candidates. Drop only floor (all four score 0%) or ceiling (all four score 100%); keep any task where models disagree, however lopsidedly -- a task only Sonnet solves is among the most informative in the set. Also sets budget caps from the slowest-converging model.
nodes.norm_label: calibration pilot and model-neutral drop rule

nodes.label: Privacy gate blocking team data collection
nodes.rationale: Engineer consent, secret-scanning over all JSONL, and a retention decision must precede any collection: retrofitting a privacy pass after twenty engineers' transcripts are in a shared bucket is far worse than doing it up front.
nodes.norm_label: privacy gate blocking team data collection

nodes.label: Task record schema (§3.7)
nodes.rationale: task_id, tier, stratum, repo, base_sha, image digest, verbatim prompt, reference_diff, f2p/p2p sets, rubric items and provenance. This is the shape task.yaml manifests implement.

nodes.label: Nine deterministic checks (resolved gate)
nodes.rationale: Run in order, first failure short-circuits and sets failure_class. `resolved` = all nine pass, binary, no partial credit -- that is what removes grader subjectivity. Deterministic checks gate; the judge only ranks, and a run failing the gate gets no quality score at all.

nodes.label: Test-file restoration from base_sha (primary anti-cheat)
nodes.rationale: Without `git checkout <base_sha> -- <test paths>` before grading, 'make the tests pass' is trivially satisfied by deleting or weakening tests, and models do this at different rates -- so it would register as a capability difference. Whether the agent modified tests is recorded separately, never silently dropped.

nodes.label: Score construction: pass@1, pass^k, paired analysis
nodes.rationale: resolve_rate is the headline and subgoal_rate breaks ties, never blended -- weighted partial credit would reintroduce the grader subjectivity all-or-nothing scoring exists to remove. Analysis is always paired: task difficulty is common to both arms and cancels in the per-task difference.
nodes.norm_label: score construction: pass@1, pass^k, paired analysis

nodes.label: Judge protocol (rubric profile + blind pairwise)
nodes.rationale: Five orthogonal dimensions on a 3-point anchored scale (1-10 scales show poor inter-rater agreement), plus round-robin blind position-randomized pairwise converted to Elo. Pair sample i against sample i -- pairing a draw against another model's best or median compares a draw to a statistic and skews the win rate.

nodes.label: Judge configuration: neutral family, evidence-fed, calibrated
nodes.rationale: A Claude judge inflates Sonnet 5 and a Gemini judge inflates Gemma, so the judge must sit outside all four families -- GPT-class, with the third-party egress tradeoff reviewed and accepted. If Cohen's kappa against the ~20% human gold subset falls below 0.6, Tier B is directional only and must not carry the decision.
nodes.norm_label: judge configuration: neutral family, evidence-fed, calibrated

nodes.label: Statistical power: why N=10, not N=3
nodes.rationale: Naive binomial CIs are optimistic and must not be quoted: attempts within a task are correlated, so the honest unpaired half-width is ~±12 pts at 60 tasks, which paired analysis brings to ~±6. Task count drives precision; N drives reliability measurement. Judge noise attenuates effects as 1/(2a-1)^2, which is why reference-anchoring and evidence-feeding are load-bearing.
nodes.norm_label: statistical power: why n=10, not n=3

nodes.label: Optional executable Tier B
nodes.rationale: Authoring acceptance tests (~1-3 hr/task) converts the primary decision signal from kappa~0.32 to deterministic -- the highest-leverage spend available. If pursued the judge is demoted, not removed: it scores attributes that resist encoding as tests and never overrides the executable result.

nodes.label: Start-state pinning (§5.1)
nodes.rationale: Every run begins from a byte-identical world: container by digest not tag, detached checkout at base_sha, lockfile dependencies baked into the image, network off or through a recording proxy, fresh container per sample. State bleed across the N=10 would correlate repeats and silently shrink effective N.

nodes.label: Claude Code configuration control (§5.2)
nodes.rationale: Named the highest-risk contamination source: CLAUDE.md, settings.json, hooks, MCP servers, skills and output styles all substantially change agent behavior, and the operator's environment is heavily customized. The verification half -- dumping and diffing the effective config at session start and storing it in the record -- is what makes the claim checkable.

nodes.label: Frozen sampling parameters (§5.3)
nodes.rationale: Temperature 0 for non-reasoning, 0.6 or lab-recommended for reasoning, recorded per run. The '(or lab-recommended)' clause is load-bearing -- what is held identical across arms is the policy, not the number.

nodes.label: Budget policy: generous caps, measure actuals (§5.4)
nodes.rationale: Caps derive from the slowest-converging model's p95 x2, not the incumbent's -- tuning to Sonnet 5's turn distribution converts a style difference into a capability score. Every cap unit favors someone (wall-clock favors fast models, turns favor verbose ones, tokens favor terse ones), so cap on turns and tokens together and record which limit terminated each run.
nodes.norm_label: budget policy: generous caps, measure actuals (§5.4)

nodes.label: Checkpointing: the cost/quality curve for free (§5.5)
nodes.rationale: One generous-cap run yields the pass rate at any budget K post-hoc -- same information as separate capped runs at half the compute. Stored as incremental diffs against base_sha, never worktrees. Grading is a decoupled offline batch because inline would be ~96,000 suite executions.
nodes.norm_label: checkpointing: the cost/quality curve for free (§5.5)

nodes.label: End-state extraction (§5.6)
nodes.rationale: `git add -A && git diff --cached <base_sha>` in the container after termination. Never trust the agent's self-report -- agents claim false success at different rates per model, which would itself become a fake signal. Staging first normalizes over whether the agent committed, left the tree dirty, or created new files.

nodes.label: Randomized, interleaved execution order (§5.7)
nodes.rationale: Sequential per-model batches confound model identity with Bedrock regional load, network conditions and host contention -- which makes latency, a stated success criterion, uninterpretable. Execution timestamp is treated as an analysis covariate.

nodes.label: Prompt-cache warming as an asymmetric cost confound (§5.8)
nodes.rationale: Sonnet 5 has prompt caching and the candidates' Bedrock cache support is unconfirmed, so batched repeats would make Sonnet artificially cheap and bias cost-per-completed-workflow against the very candidates the eval exists to evaluate. Controls: interleave, log cache_state.warm and the prior same-task run id, report cost both raw and cache-normalized.
nodes.norm_label: prompt-cache warming as an asymmetric cost confound (§5.8)

nodes.label: Per-run record (§6.1)
nodes.rationale: The full field list the harness dataclasses implement: versions block, config digest, timing split into inference vs tool_exec, per-turn token records required for the cost-at-budget-K curve, checkpoints, tool call stats, failure_class, destructive events, host metrics and artifact paths.

nodes.label: Mandatory wire-level logging (§6.2)
nodes.rationale: Without the full pre-parse request/response payload, `malformed: true` is a dead end -- you cannot tell whether the fault was LiteLLM's tool translation or the model. That distinction is the difference between 'fix the adapter and retest' and 'drop the model', the single most consequential call the eval has to make.

nodes.label: Judge and human-grader records (§6.3)
nodes.rationale: Stored separately and linked by run_id, carrying the exact input_payload and shown_payload. Without those and time_spent_s a disputed kappa cannot be re-examined -- and because judge inputs are logged, swapping the judge is a re-score rather than a re-run.

nodes.label: Exclusion policy (§6.4)
nodes.rationale: Exclusion is the one mechanism by which results get massaged, even honestly. Criteria are written down before the run, every excluded run keeps its full record, and the exclusion rate is reported per model because asymmetry is itself a finding.

nodes.label: Adapter-failure exclusion class
nodes.rationale: Genuinely ambiguous: adapter failures are fixable going forward AND they are the production path. So headline results are published with and without them, always both, never collapsed into one number.

nodes.label: Logger verification gate (§6.6 fault injection)
nodes.rationale: Twelve fault-injection cases that must each produce a complete, correctly-classified record. The logger is trusted with 2,400 runs, so it is tested before rather than after. Closed 2026-08-06; working the list found four defects the originally-drafted tests would have passed over.

nodes.label: Phase plan 0 through 6
nodes.rationale: Deliberately reordered so data capture precedes scoring -- scoring reads the log and never gates collection. Total ~3.5-4.5 weeks against the plan doc's 2.5-3; the delta is the instrumentation phase and N=10, which are what make the result defensible.

nodes.label: Phase 0c end-to-end smoke test (go/no-go)
nodes.rationale: If a candidate cannot drive Claude Code at all through LiteLLM, that must surface on day one rather than in week three after the dataset is built. A failure is not necessarily disqualifying -- it may be an adapter issue -- but it changes the plan immediately. Also sizes the compute plan.

nodes.label: Cost baseline open item (§8)
nodes.rationale: The plan's $5,000/month baseline assumes zero caching, but a representative transcript record shows ~99.99% of input billed as cache reads at 0.1x list. If candidates lack Bedrock caching while the baseline has it, true savings is materially smaller and possibly small enough to change the recommendation -- a blocking input, not a footnote.

nodes.label: Stated limitations (§9)
nodes.rationale: To appear in the writeup, not buried: autonomous single-instruction is harder than real usage (a lower bound), the task set is Pindrop-specific by intent, Tier B judgment is low-resolution by nature, harness fit is confounded with capability, and transcript-derived tasks skew toward already-agent-suitable work.

nodes.label: Scorecard, not a composite (§10)
nodes.rationale: Collapsing rows into one number hides the tradeoff and renders the result unfalsifiable; a scorecard forces the tradeoff into the open where it can be argued with. Any metric reported without a confidence interval is not reported.

nodes.label: Reference points, not gates (OPEN-8)
nodes.rationale: Four of six thresholds are defaults with nothing behind them, so they are annotations on the scorecard rather than pass/fail criteria. Promotion to decision criteria must happen before results exist, never after.

nodes.label: OPEN-10 destructive-event severity scale
nodes.rationale: §6.1 used `severity` without defining levels. Resolution: high = unreverted data/history loss or secret exposure, medium = reverted or contained, low = risky but no effect.

nodes.label: Storage (§6.5)
nodes.rationale: Gzipped trajectories and wire logs, incremental checkpoint diffs, container stdout/stderr, test output and full judge records -- low tens of GB for 2,400 runs, cheap insurance relative to re-running. Private repo or bucket with a documented access list, secret-scanned on write because wire logs and trajectories both contain repository source.

nodes.label: Bakeoff Harness & Logging Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Tasks 1-12 building the instrumented run harness. Scoring is deliberately absent -- this plan produces the raw record that later plans derive scores from. Every module owns one responsibility and is testable without Docker except container, claude_runner and runner.

nodes.label: Task 1: Schema and append-only event log
nodes.rationale: Records open with mode 'x' so overwriting is impossible; the index is appended only after the record is fsynced and atomically renamed, so the index never advertises a run that does not exist. No update or delete API exists anywhere in the package -- excluded runs keep their records.
nodes.norm_label: task 1: schema and append-only event log

nodes.label: Task 2: Cost calculation and PRICE_BOOK
nodes.rationale: Candidate cache multipliers are explicitly None rather than guessed: AWS publishes no cache pricing for any of the three, and guessing would silently corrupt the headline cost metric, so observed cache tokens raise instead.

nodes.label: Price correction 2026-08-05: Kimi output $3.00 not $2.50
nodes.rationale: The plan doc had taken the optimistic end of Model_Bakeoff_Plan.md's '$2.50-3.00' range; re-verifying all four against the AWS pricing page corrected it, along with the 3.10 -> 3.60 test expectation.

nodes.label: Task 3: Tolerant trajectory parser
nodes.rationale: Parsing is deliberately tolerant: a run killed mid-write leaves a partial final line, and losing the whole trajectory over one truncated line would violate the spec's no-data-loss requirement. Malformed lines are counted, not swallowed.

nodes.label: Timing correction: inference_ms vs tool_exec_ms must partition the span
nodes.rationale: Measuring inference as the gap between consecutive assistant records folds tool execution into it and leaves tool_exec_ms permanently zero -- against the fixture that left 5s of 30s unaccounted. A split that cannot distinguish a slow model from a slow test run makes the latency success criterion unusable. Tool-result records carry timestamps, so the real split is already in the transcript.
nodes.norm_label: timing correction: inference_ms vs tool_exec_ms must partition the span

nodes.label: Task 4: Destructive-command and secret scanners
nodes.rationale: reverted_by_agent and affected_outcome are hardcoded False, so severity is permanently HIGH and OPEN-10's MEDIUM tier is unreachable at scan time. Revert detection needs checkpoint file state; inferring it from the bash stream alone would miss Write-tool restores and produce false MEDIUM downgrades, so conservative HIGH is the right default and a test pins the unresolved status.

nodes.label: Task 5: Container lifecycle and git pinning
nodes.rationale: Digest-pinned image, detached checkout, snapshot_diff and restore_paths. Every git call routes through _checked_exec because a failed `git diff` returns empty output byte-identical to a clean tree. The digest check accepts a bare sha256: image id since a locally built image has no registry digest.
nodes.norm_label: task 5: container lifecycle and git pinning

nodes.label: macOS bind-mount hazard (empty mount reads as clean tree)
nodes.rationale: The Docker VM mounts $HOME but not /var/folders where pytest's tmp_path lives, so the repo mounts as an empty directory with no error and git's 'not a git repository' goes to stderr. Snapshot tests then compare nothing against nothing and pass. Fixed by --basetemp under $HOME plus direct mount and git-availability assertions.
nodes.norm_label: macos bind-mount hazard (empty mount reads as clean tree)

nodes.label: Task 6: Live checkpoint capture
nodes.rationale: Capture happens on stdout turn boundaries while the agent works, so staging must go to a throwaway GIT_INDEX_FILE -- staging under a live agent means a later agent commit sweeps in files it never staged and its git status disagrees with reality. Boundary precision is approximate by however long a snapshot takes, recorded rather than hidden.

nodes.label: Checkpoint off-by-one: report turns completed, not announced
nodes.rationale: An assistant message announces the tool calls a turn is about to make, so at message k the tree still holds k-1 turns of work. Firing on_turn(k) there files turn k-1's work under turn k and understates every checkpoint by one -- on the exact axis the cost-at-budget-K curve is plotted against.
nodes.norm_label: checkpoint off-by-one: report turns completed, not announced

nodes.label: Task 7: Wire-level logging and litellm config
nodes.rationale: Both transports are configured so Phase 0 can pick per arm from evidence and an adapter failure can be told apart from model weakness. Every model_name is distinct on purpose -- LiteLLM round-robins repeated names, which would randomize transport per call and confound latency and tool-translation results -- and model_name doubles as the PRICE_BOOK key.
nodes.norm_label: task 7: wire-level logging and litellm config

nodes.label: LiteLLM callbacks must be CustomLogger instances
nodes.rationale: success_handler dispatches on isinstance(callback, CustomLogger), so a duck-typed object is skipped in silence -- no wire log, no error, against a mandatory requirement. Worse, get_instance_fn resolves a dotted path with getattr and returns it as-is, so a path to a class lands the class object in the callback list and fails the same check. The fix is a dotted path to a module-level instance.
nodes.norm_label: litellm callbacks must be customlogger instances

nodes.label: Task 8: Failure and exclusion classification
nodes.rationale: Produces RunSignals, classify_failure, classify_exclusion and a pre-registered reason-code set, per the spec's requirement that exclusion criteria are written down before the run begins.

nodes.label: FALSE_SUCCESS correction: tests_passed is None, not False
nodes.rationale: With tests_passed hardcoded False, the normal healthy path -- agent finishes, no malformation, no truncation, no loop -- reached `agent_claimed_success and not tests_passed` and stamped FALSE_SUCCESS, an accusation of dishonesty, on every clean run. Grading is offline, so the harness must not pre-judge: None means unknown.
nodes.norm_label: false_success correction: tests_passed is none, not false

nodes.label: Task 9: Claude Code runner and config isolation
nodes.rationale: Builds the command, env and config_digest against claude 2.1.220. --max-turns exists but is hidden from --help, verified by inspecting the binary rather than assumed.
nodes.norm_label: task 9: claude code runner and config isolation

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, not --settings, detaches user config
nodes.rationale: --settings loads ADDITIONAL settings on top of ~/.claude/settings.json, and --strict-mcp-config covers MCP servers only -- leaving hooks, skills, output styles, plugins and user CLAUDE.md in place. The plan had also stripped CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, which makes the CLI fall back to ~/.claude: the lever pulled the wrong way. Setting it to an empty per-run directory relocates all of it at once.

nodes.label: Environment is an allowlist, not a denylist
nodes.rationale: A denylist over the inherited env missed the load-bearing case: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK and _USE_VERTEX make the CLI ignore ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, bypass the proxy and leave the mandatory wire log empty while the run looks normal. An allowlist fails closed.
nodes.norm_label: environment is an allowlist, not a denylist

nodes.label: Per-run transcript discovery
nodes.rationale: Returning the newest *.jsonl in the project dir lets a run that crashes before writing inherit the previous model's trajectory, tokens and cost. The munging rule was also wrong -- Claude Code hyphenates dots as well as separators -- so any repo path with a dot resolved to a nonexistent directory and recorded zeros without complaint. Both close by globbing the per-run config dir.

nodes.label: Temperature is per-model and excluded from config_digest
nodes.rationale: A single uniform temperature would 400 every call on the reference arm (Sonnet 5 rejects non-default sampling) and convert Kimi's documented temperature-0 stall into a latency measurement. Folding a necessarily-per-model value into a cross-arm identity digest would make the digest assert something false.
nodes.norm_label: temperature is per-model and excluded from config_digest

nodes.label: Task 10: Run orchestrator (execute_run)
nodes.rationale: Composes Tasks 1-9 into one run producing exactly one record. Closing its eleven carried-forward defects changed the architecture twice: the agent moved inside the container, and checkpoints moved to live capture.

nodes.label: Internal Docker network with the proxy as a peer
nodes.rationale: 'Agent in the container' and network_mode=none were mutually exclusive; §5.1's 'or through a recording proxy' branch resolves it. An internal=True network has no host route, so 127.0.0.1:4000 is unreachable by design and the proxy must run as a container on that network. Asserting only that the internet is blocked would pass on a container with no network at all -- the one configuration the agent cannot work under.
nodes.norm_label: internal docker network with the proxy as a peer

nodes.label: Defect 12: api_error_status never populated
nodes.rationale: execute_run never passed it to assemble_record, so the throttle/5xx exclusion branch was unreachable and every Bedrock 429 was scored against the model. The drafted test called classify_exclusion directly and passed green over the dead path. Now derived from the wire log, counting only the last call and only if it failed.

nodes.label: Defect 13: version block 4/6 empty on every record
nodes.rationale: litellm, bedrock_model_id, harness_commit and task_set_commit were empty strings on every record written. Now from importlib.metadata (litellm.__version__ does not exist in 1.95.0 and raises AttributeError), git rev-parse with a -dirty suffix, and the resolved model read off the wire.
nodes.norm_label: defect 13: version block 4/6 empty on every record

nodes.label: Defect 14: checkpoints discarded on mid-run failure
nodes.rationale: `checkpoints = recorder.captured` sat inside the try, so any mid-run failure threw away every checkpoint already captured and the record still looked well-formed -- an empty checkpoint list is indistinguishable from a quiet run. The recorder is now held outside the try and read in the finally.
nodes.norm_label: defect 14: checkpoints discarded on mid-run failure

nodes.label: Defect 15: wire capture registered in the wrong process
nodes.rationale: Callbacks registered in the harness process, which makes no LLM calls -- the agent runs in its own container and the model call is made by the proxy, a third process. Every real run would have produced an empty wire log and with it empty sampling and hashes, silently. Closed by moving capture into the proxy and replaying those lines through the existing WireLogger so there is still one canonical artifact.
nodes.norm_label: defect 15: wire capture registered in the wrong process

nodes.label: Task 11: Fault-injection gate (verify_logger.py)
nodes.rationale: With no Docker daemon the gate returns GATE INCOMPLETE and exit 1, not a pass: half of §6.6 is only observable against a real daemon, and reporting 'passed' on the strength of checks that cannot see those is the exact failure the gate exists to prevent. Includes a negative control so the positive capture test cannot pass on in-process capture.

nodes.label: Task 12: End-to-end smoke test (Phase 0c)
nodes.rationale: Offline half done 2026-08-06: real Claude Code binary, pinned container, real proxy on an internal network, real streaming SSE from a stub -- 3 turns, 2 tool calls, a 157-byte staged diff, zero unattributed calls. Building it turned up four more defects none of the existing tests could see.

nodes.label: Defect 16: production proxy config registered no wire callback
nodes.rationale: Defect 15 in a second place: every real run would have read an empty wire directory. The config comment argued correctly about a dotted path to a class; the fix is a path to a module-level instance.
nodes.norm_label: defect 16: production proxy config registered no wire callback

nodes.label: Defect 17: eval_settings.json was mounted nowhere
nodes.rationale: --settings named a path no image had, and Claude Code does not fail on a missing settings file -- it starts with none of the pinned settings, the agent cannot edit anything, and a one-line harness omission reads as four capability findings.

nodes.label: Defect 18: the image ran as root
nodes.rationale: Claude Code refuses bypassPermissions under root and --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions does not lift the guard. Visible only after defect 17 was fixed; together the two would have landed no diff on any arm.
nodes.norm_label: defect 18: the image ran as root

nodes.label: Defect 19: mock deployments never exercise the streaming path
nodes.rationale: mock_response short-circuits inside anthropic_messages before litellm's streaming wrapper, so the success callback never fires for a streaming request -- and every real Claude Code call is streaming. Measured: two calls served, one captured. The gate now cross-checks its own capture against the proxy's access log.
nodes.norm_label: defect 19: mock deployments never exercise the streaming path

nodes.label: Sonnet 5 tokenizer asymmetry in uniform token budgets
nodes.rationale: Sonnet 5's tokenizer produces ~30% more tokens for the same text, so a uniform output-token cap gives it ~30% less text budget than the other arms -- a config choice scored as a capability difference -- and cost-per-task is not directly comparable at equal text. Left to the calibration pilot, where cap derivation belongs.
nodes.norm_label: sonnet 5 tokenizer asymmetry in uniform token budgets

nodes.label: Gate 1 — the real-task input path
nodes.rationale: One real issue, end to end, on all four arms, with a precondition strong enough that a failure is attributable to the model. Implemented 2026-08-12 at schema 3.5.0; §6 is a three-pass review log of what the plan got wrong before any code was written.

nodes.label: Root cause A: no precondition on the harness INPUT
nodes.rationale: Every existing check is about the harness or a run's output; nothing asserts the thing handed to the agent is a task at all. That defect invalidated every Phase 0c capability figure. Six of six 'model failures' so far were harness defects -- the base rate is the argument for a gate that runs offline before any spend.
nodes.norm_label: root cause a: no precondition on the harness input

nodes.label: Root cause B: operational knowledge lived in a script
nodes.rationale: smoke_test.py was the only place that knew the proxy topology, credential paths, image build and config dump. A matrix driver beside it would either duplicate that knowledge -- so the gate and the real run drift into different environments and the gate stops gating -- or reach into a script from library code. Extraction into proxy.py and session.py is what keeps them one environment.
nodes.norm_label: root cause b: operational knowledge lived in a script

nodes.label: Task on disk: task.yaml plus reference.diff
nodes.rationale: One reference diff split at load, never two hand-maintained files. Two properties fall out and both are checked: the halves recompose to the original byte for byte, so nothing can be silently dropped; and a file that is neither half is a load error rather than a quiet omission.
nodes.norm_label: task on disk: task.yaml plus reference.diff

nodes.label: Start state is base_sha plus the committed test half
nodes.rationale: A real bug-fix PR carries the test that proves the fix, and at base_sha that oracle does not exist -- so the self-correction loop has nothing to run against, the same truncation that invalidated Phase 0c arriving through the dataset instead of the image. Recorded as a methodology decision: handing over the oracle makes the task 'make this test pass', while a hidden oracle makes difficulty depend on the agent's test-writing habits. The setup commit uses a fixed author/date/message so start_sha is a pure function of the manifest and can be pinned.
nodes.norm_label: start state is base_sha plus the committed test half

nodes.label: Generated per-task Dockerfile
nodes.rationale: Generated rather than hand-written because the two most expensive ways a task image can be wrong are structural and a generator makes them impossible: USER root makes Claude Code refuse bypassPermissions, and an inherited ENTRYPOINT turns the container's sleep into an immediate exit. Both read as total model failure. `pip install -e .` is required -- a non-editable install resolves imports to site-packages so the agent's edits do nothing and every arm fails identically.

nodes.label: Preflight: the per-task discrimination precondition
nodes.rationale: Offline, no credentials, no spend, per task before the matrix starts: red before the reference fix and green after it, in this task's own image. The load-bearing detail is the exit code -- pytest's 1 means tests ran and failed while 2/3/4/5 mean the environment is broken, so `returncode != 0` would accept the exact Phase 0c failure as evidence the bug is present. Also checks non-root, claude version, git/rg, empty entrypoint, a clean tree after the suite, and no task-local CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Matrix driver: round-major ordering, resume, containment
nodes.rationale: Every (task, arm) appears once per round, shuffled under a recorded seed, so repeats are separated by a whole round -- the strongest separation available -- while staying reproducible. Resume is mandatory rather than nice, because run_id is deterministic and write_run opens mode 'x', so a second invocation against the same log raises. One cell's exception must not cost the other 2,399 and must not be swallowed either.
nodes.norm_label: matrix driver: round-major ordering, resume, containment

nodes.label: Resume guard on task_version and image digest
nodes.rationale: task_version is not part of run_id, so editing a task and re-running leaves every existing cell looking complete and silently mixes records of the old and new task under one task_id -- the most damaging hole in draft 1, and exactly the class Gate 1 exists to close. Version mismatch is a hard per-cell refusal; image-digest mismatch only warns behind --allow-mixed-images, because images legitimately rebuild and refusing would make resume useless.
nodes.norm_label: resume guard on task_version and image digest

nodes.label: What the matrix gates on vs. what the smoke test gates on
nodes.rationale: smoke_test's run_problems is the Phase 0c capability criterion, where no diff is a NO-GO. The matrix asks a different question -- a model failing a task is the data it is collecting -- so the driver checks only what makes a record uninterpretable (config dump, empty wire log, lost attribution, isolated=False) and never stops a run from being written.
nodes.norm_label: what the matrix gates on vs. what the smoke test gates on

nodes.label: task_set_commit and the 3.4.0 version bump
nodes.rationale: SCHEMA_VERSION moves even though no field is added: in 3.3.0 an empty task_set_commit means 'no dataset exists', in 3.4.0 it means 'this task declared none'. Same bytes, different claim -- the case the versioning rule exists for. A defect in the plan's own dirty-marker (a relative pathspec matching nothing) was caught by running it, not by reading it.

nodes.label: First real task: pallets/click #3360 / PR #3434
nodes.rationale: Chosen because its tests assert rendered behavior rather than an internal name, so a different-but-correct fix passes -- the rejected alternative (#3678) pins an arbitrary storage name and would score a correct alternative fix as a failure. Hermetic and fast (1,614 tests in 1.4s), and unlike the fixture it forces real navigation. It also surfaced that per-task dependency pinning is mandatory: the suite does not collect under the base image's pytest 9.1.1.

nodes.label: Pruned-Mirror Handoff Closeout Plan
nodes.rationale: Closes HANDOFF.md: six shipped prose defects, four deferred code fixes (lock, streaming object sweep, utf-8 git output, cache permissions), two uncovered lines, and the docs. Every change stays inside ensure_pruned_mirror and its neighbours; all git behavior claims were measured on darwin/APFS/git 2.50.1 during plan review.

nodes.label: Mutation anchors constrain how the code may be edited
nodes.rationale: mutation_check.py matches exact source substrings including leading indentation and reports STALE ANCHOR otherwise. Six anchors live inside ensure_pruned_mirror's body, which is why the lock is added by extracting the body into a helper rather than wrapping it in a `with` -- re-indenting the region would stale all six.
nodes.norm_label: mutation anchors constrain how the code may be edited

nodes.label: _build_pruned_mirror as a seam, not a decomposition
nodes.rationale: The body moves verbatim and unre-indented so every mutation anchor inside it survives byte-for-byte; inlining it back 'for tidiness' stales all six. Its docstring says so, because the wrapper's comment is not where someone editing the body looks.
nodes.norm_label: _build_pruned_mirror as a seam, not a decomposition

nodes.label: One flock per repo slug
nodes.rationale: Closes three readers: the mirror fetch path (clone writes HEAD early so a second process fetches into a half-populated clone), the prune build-and-publish, and materialize's run-tree clone (the publish rmtree's the directory that clone is reading). Per slug, not per (repo, base_sha), because both keys share one source mirror and one sweep namespace. flock self-conflicts across two fds in one process, so the acquisitions must not nest. The lock file is never unlinked -- removing one another process holds open silently breaks exclusion for every later acquirer.

nodes.label: _commits_outside streams one past its sample
nodes.rationale: Buffering the whole --batch-all-objects listing was 659 KB on pruned click and ~229 MB extrapolated to a 5M-object monorepo, for a message that prints three names. Reading ONE past the sample is what lets the message distinguish 'exactly N' from 'more than N' -- 3 outside commits (a ref-sweep miss) and 30,000 (a gc that did nothing) are different diagnoses, and absence-is-recorded forbids rendering them identically.

nodes.label: _git decodes pinned utf-8 with replacement
nodes.rationale: text=True decodes with the process locale and errors='strict', so one non-UTF-8 byte in git output -- or LC_ALL=C on a CI runner -- raised UnicodeDecodeError naming neither the repo nor the task. The old 'a mangled ref gets deleted, the safe direction' claim was measured false: the ref sweep deletes by decoded name and update-ref --stdin exits 0 on a nonexistent ref, so the real ref survives and _verify_pruned's object sweep refuses the mirror. Loud refusal, not a leak.

nodes.label: Published mirror keeps mkdtemp's 0700
nodes.rationale: The fix is a deletion, not a chmod: the rmtree existed on a claim that clone 'tolerates an empty target only if it does not exist', measured false -- git 2.50.1 clones into an existing empty directory and keeps its mode. Without it the clone recreates the directory under the umask and os.replace publishes a world-readable cache permanently. The test pins umask(0) so the verdict is the repository's, not the laptop's.

nodes.label: A damaged prune cache rebuilds rather than raises
nodes.rationale: Raising left the damaged entry on disk, unmaterializable until an operator deleted it by hand -- three identical TaskErrors measured, with a message that reads like a prune bug and no instruction to delete anything. The rebuild's own post-condition on the tmp it just built still raises and still gates the rename: refusing a prune this code built is a code defect, refusing one it found on disk is a cache defect, and only the second is recoverable.
nodes.norm_label: a damaged prune cache rebuilds rather than raises

nodes.label: Publish TaskError must not name reclaimed paths
nodes.rationale: The message said 'the build itself succeeded and is at {tmp}' while the finally-block rmtree reclaims tmp as the exception propagates. Rewording rather than preserving tmp is right: tmp and dest are siblings so EXDEV is impossible and ENOSPC is the live failure, where stranding a full mirror makes the problem worse. It also must not tell the operator to act on dest, which on the second os.replace has itself been renamed aside.
nodes.norm_label: publish taskerror must not name reclaimed paths

nodes.label: The base_sha guard exists for a NAMED failure, not a vacuous pass
nodes.rationale: The shipped claim -- that without the cat-file -e guard _commits_outside passes vacuously on an empty store -- is false: _ancestors runs rev-list under check=True and raises first. What the caller loses is the message, since _git's generic exit-128 line names neither the mirror nor the fact that this is a cache defect. The same false claim shipped in three places at once.
nodes.norm_label: the base_sha guard exists for a named failure, not a vacuous pass

nodes.label: The stale-tmp sweep skips an unstatable entry
nodes.rationale: The sweep stats entries it did not create in a cache directory shared by every repo, so an entry can vanish between the glob and the stat when another invocation reclaims it first. That OSError must mean 'skip', never 'fail the build': the sweep only reclaims disk, and a build that dies on someone else's leftover turns a janitor into a single point of failure.
nodes.norm_label: the stale-tmp sweep skips an unstatable entry
